summary.text: Ionic bonding is the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal so that both atoms end up with a full valence shell.
The electrostatic attraction between the resulting anions and cations builds a solid lattice in which the ions are stacked in an alternating fashion.
Ionic compounds generally have a high melting point and conduct electricity when molten or in solution, but typically not when solid.

facts.label: Table salt
facts.value: Sodium atoms lose an electron and chlorine atoms gain one, in a 1:1 ratio

facts.label: Bond energy
facts.value: Ionic bonds have high bond energy and are among the strongest bonds

facts.label: Conducts when
facts.value: Molten or dissolved in water, typically not when solid

facts.label: Never purely ionic
facts.value: All ionic compounds have some degree of electron sharing

facts.label: Crystal structure
facts.value: Ions stack in an alternating lattice with no discrete molecules

items.prompt: A chemist dissolves a white crystal in water and the liquid now carries an electric current. What is the best explanation?

options.label: The lattice broke apart and free ions can carry charge
The water joined the crystal's atoms into long chains
Water supplied a sea of electrons that the crystal lacked
The dissolved atoms became neutral molecules that conduct

items.explain: Ionic compounds break up into ions in water, and these free ions make the solution a good conductor.

items.prompt: A lithium-like metal atom meets a chlorine-like nonmetal atom. Which description fits how they bond ionically?

options.label: They pool their electrons into a shared sea of metal
They split a pair of electrons evenly between them
The metal gives up an electron and the nonmetal takes it
The nonmetal gives up an electron and the metal takes it

items.explain: Ionic bonds result from the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal, forming a cation and an anion.

items.prompt: A bond forms between two atoms with a huge gap in how strongly they pull on electrons. How would a chemist classify it?

options.label: Ionic, since the polarity is greater than any covalent character
Metallic, since the electrons are pulled away entirely
Purely covalent, since the electrons are shared equally
A weak bond, since the pull on electrons is uneven

items.explain: The term ionic bonding is used when the ionic character is greater than the covalent character, which happens with a large electronegativity difference.

items.prompt: Two ionic solids differ only in that one is built from ions with larger charges. Which is likely to melt at the higher temperature?

options.label: The one with smaller charges, since it is less tightly packed
The one with larger charges, since its cohesive forces are stronger
Neither, since melting depends only on the metal's weight
They melt together, since ionic charge never changes melting

items.explain: The higher the charges, the stronger the cohesive forces and the higher the melting point.

items.prompt: A student draws one NaCl molecule as a tiny pair of atoms, like a drawn dumbbell. What is wrong with this picture of solid salt?

options.label: Solid salt is really a metal, so it has no ions to draw
Sodium and chlorine can never be drawn next to each other
Solid salt is pure covalent sharing, with no charges at all
Ions stack in a lattice where separate molecular units cannot be told apart

items.explain: In an ionic lattice it is usually not possible to distinguish discrete molecular units, so the compounds are not molecular.

items.prompt: Why do atoms with an almost empty outer shell, like sodium, readily form positive ions?

options.label: They have few outer electrons that are easily lost to others
They pull on extra electrons more strongly than other atoms
They are held to nearby atoms by a rigid lattice from the start
They hold their electrons very tightly, so they fill the shell

items.explain: Weakly electronegative atoms such as alkali metals have relatively few valence electrons, which are easily lost to strongly electronegative atoms, forming cations.
